identification: 4 boxes of toys (description 'model cars etc'). Re-viewed all 6 photos full size and zoomed. (1) Boxed FROG 'Buccaneer' Ready to Fly model, rubber-powered, red and yellow plastic plane, box lid reads FROG / 'Buccaneer' / Ready to Fly Model (International Model Aircraft, UK, 1960s, cat no 318F). Photo 3 shows it open with the red fuselage, yellow wings, propeller, winder and instruction sheet inside, so it looks complete. (2) Red tin-litho truck about 30-35cm long with extending ladder section, roof beacon, striped bumper, cab badge reads 'SUPER' and side text partly legible, Japanese friction/battery type, no maker mark legible (Kokyu-style ladder truck). (3) Small yellow plastic and tin-litho airliner with N801E (a Delta DC-8 registration) on wing and fuselage, Japanese tin/plastic type, common. (4) Another boxed toy on top of the pile, a battery-operated toy whose title is not legible ('Harness...' or similar), so unidentified. (5) A framed item, a box of larger plastic toys and loose play-worn diecast and plastic cars (a tub and a box, Matchbox/Hot Wheels/Majorette type), common.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 20-30, current bid $90 (rechecked 9 Nov, up from $20 at the ID pass, so others have noticed the plane). The Buccaneer is the value: complete boxed examples sold for about A$70-170 on eBay UK (fixed price) and about A$30-75 at auction; most are within 3 years and prices are steady, with ten of the 20 or so sales in 2025-26. Andy should check at the viewing that the plane is complete (propeller, wings, winder, instruction sheet, oil bottle) and the box is intact. The truck: Japanese ladder trucks sell A$24-135 depending on maker, working friction and condition; check for a maker mark on the underside, missing ladder parts and rust. Unidentified boxed battery toy on top may add value, ask for a look. Loose cars look common. Buyer's premium 22% on top of the bid. Postage on the plane and truck is moderate. Note Terapeak UK prices are converted to AUD and exclude postage; resale buyers are mostly UK.
